stories.name: Isa Okonkwo
stories.profession: Education consultant; proprietor of Dar ibn Taimiyyah Islamic Homeschool
stories.summary: In a 2024 interview with The PUNCH, Isa Okonkwo publicly described growing up in an Igbo family in Nkanu West, researching Islam as a teenager, accepting Islam by personal conviction, and later attending an Islamic school in Afikpo, Ebonyi State.
stories.source_title: Hoarding Sallah meat from neighbours sinful – Igbo Islamic cleric

stories.name: Zubair Ugwu
stories.profession: Not stated in the cited report
stories.summary: In a PREMIUM TIMES interview published in 2021, Zubair Ugwu publicly identified as an Igbo Muslim from Alor-Agu in Igbo-Eze South, Enugu State. The report states that he attended schools outside the South-East where he converted to Islam; Ugwu then personally described returning to the East and being labelled a saboteur because he identified as Muslim.
stories.source_title: Inside the world of Igbo Muslims in Nigeria’s South-east region

stories.name: Aisha Suleiman
stories.summary: In a Daily Trust/Trust Radio interview, Aisha Suleiman, formerly Josephine Oziomachukwu Nworie, publicly said she converted to Islam about five years before the 2023 interview. She identified her family as Igbo from Awgu Local Government Area of Enugu State and described her reasons for embracing Islam and her continuing commitment despite family opposition.
stories.source_title: Despite challenges, I’ve no regret embracing Islam – Igbo Christian convert

stories.name: Yusuf Onumaegbu
stories.profession: Traditional ruler, Eze Amara I of Amaano Ovungwo
stories.summary: In a 2024 interview with The PUNCH, Yusuf Onumaegbu publicly said he embraced Islam about 49 years earlier while working in northern Nigeria. He said reading Islamic books and the Qur’an and his interactions with Muslims led to his decision. He identified himself as Eze Amara I of Amaano Ovungwo in Isiala Ngwa South, Abia State.
stories.source_title: Why we profess Islam despite discrimination in S’East – Igbo Muslims

stories.name: Musa Dimunah
stories.town: Not stated in the cited report
stories.profession: Traditional ruler; Vice Chairman of the Council of Village Heads in Imo State
stories.summary: In a telephone interview originally reported by OnIslam and preserved by Alukah, Imo traditional ruler Sylvester O. Dimunah, who took the name Musa Dimunah, publicly described embracing Islam and said his decision followed his own study of the religion and his positive impressions of Muslim conduct. Anadolu Agency independently reported in August 2013 that the Imo monarch had converted earlier that year.

research.title: Being Igbo and Muslim: The Igbo of South-Eastern Nigeria and Conversions to Islam, 1930s to Recent Times
research.publisher: The Journal of African History / Cambridge University Press

research.title: The Stages of Igbo Conversion to Islam: An Empirical Study
